scenes.headline: How WorldClaw builds 3D worlds by writing Blender programs
scenes.sub: Tencent Hunyuan's agentic pipeline: plan, terrain, objects, refine.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Raisin! WorldClaw turns a text prompt into a whole explorable 3D world. The trick: it doesn't generate 3D. It writes programs that do.

scenes.text: The agent's output is executable Blender code: terrain as noise and landform programs, objects as meshes placed by solved transforms.
scenes.say: Every stage hands Blender a program, so the world comes out as named regions and separate objects you can open and edit.

steps.say: A planning agent turns the prompt into a structured spec: regions, terrain conditions and objects.
Terrain is built first. Then regions that need detail get objects conditioned on it, so a hut already knows its slope.
Agents render, inspect and refine, because a wrong number in a program is a mountain in the wrong place.

scenes.title: One height field, written per region
scenes.text: H(x) = Σ m_r(x) · [h_r + Σ w N + Σ α G]

parts.match: [h_r + Σ w N + Σ α G]
parts.note: base height, noise octaves, landforms like peaks and dunes
parts.say: Each region adds a base height, weighted noise, and landforms like peaks, craters and dunes.

parts.note: normalized masks: they sum to one everywhere
parts.say: A mask gates each region, and the masks sum to one everywhere. So a beach blends into a forest, with no seam.

scenes.say: The terrain is one field, authored region by region.

items.text: Render the terrain, draw the scene
items.say: For a region, render the terrain and generate an image of what should stand on it.
Segment each object out, and rebuild it as a textured mesh.
Solve its scale from depths and focal lengths, then a rotation and position. Its base may sink slightly into a slope, but never float.

scenes.quote: fully validating this decoupled pipeline at the current stage still requires capable models such as Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-Image-2, and Hunyuan3D.
scenes.say: The paper is candid about the catch. Its executable stages need frontier models, and every comparison it offers is judged by eye, with no scores.

scenes.text: Make the output a program instead of pixels or a field, and the generated world stays editable afterwards.

recap: Plan, then terrain, then objects on it
Masks that sum to one blend regions
scenes.say: To recap: plan first, blend the terrain, and solve where every object stands.
